This chapter demonstrates the executable-source contract. The `.qmd` file is authoritative; its generated Markdown and figure are reviewed and versioned for stable web and PDF builds.

## A reproducible Python figure

The example uses fixed input values and an explicit plotting seed so repeated renders produce the same analytical result.

```{python}
#| label: fig-python-trend
#| fig-cap: "Deterministic trend generated with Python"
#| fig-alt: "A line chart increasing from one to five across five observations"

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

x = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
y = [1, 2, 2, 4, 5]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4))
ax.plot(x, y, marker="o", color="#31688e", linewidth=2)
ax.set(xlabel="Observation", ylabel="Value")
ax.grid(alpha=0.25)
plt.show()
```

The committed figure makes the result inspectable without executing Python during an ordinary Jekyll build.
